title: [mobile] 3 navigation link(s) disappear at 390px and no menu button brings them back
detail: At a phone viewport the header hides its navigation links and puts nothing in their place. There is no menu button: the links are in the markup, so every static check passes, but a media query paints them out and nothing brings them back. The header collapses to a logo and the rest of the site becomes unreachable from the top of the page. Most traffic to a site like this is on a phone. The header offers 4 destination(s) at the desktop viewport and 1 at 390px. There is no menu button in the header: no button, no aria-expanded, no aria-controls, nothing named like a menu anywhere on the page. The links are simply painted out by a media query with nothing put in their place. 3 of them are still reachable further down the page (typically the footer), so navigating means scrolling to the bottom of every page.
remedy: Add the menu button the responsive layout assumes exists: a <button aria-expanded aria-controls> in the header, shown only below the breakpoint that hides the links, which toggles a panel containing them. Keeping the links in the footer is not a substitute -- it makes every navigation a scroll to the bottom of the page.

instances.message: The primary navigation. Look for the breakpoint class on the wrapper around the links -- a "hidden md:flex" or equivalent hides them below the tablet width.
instances.expected: 4 destination(s), or a menu button that reveals them
